tools.name: query
tools.title: Run read-only SQL
tools.description: Run one read-only SQL statement against the connected PostgreSQL database and get rows back as JSON. Send exactly one statement per call (SELECT, WITH, EXPLAIN, or SHOW). It runs inside an engine-enforced read-only transaction, so any write is refused by the database. Use this tool for all data reading, aggregation, and query planning. Returns {rows, rowCount, returnedRows, truncated}, plus hint when truncated is true. Prefer $1, $2 placeholders with the params array over interpolating values. Results are capped at ~32768 bytes; truncated:true means rows were dropped - add LIMIT/WHERE or select fewer columns.

sql.description: One SQL statement. Use $1, $2, ... for parameters.

params.description: Positional parameter values bound to $1, $2, ... placeholders.

tools.name: execute
tools.title: Run a write statement (disabled)
tools.description: Run a data-modifying SQL statement (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE or DDL). Currently DISABLED: the server is read-only, so this returns an error and changes nothing. To enable writes, the operator must start the server with PG_ALLOW_WRITE=true.

sql.description: One INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DDL statement. Use $1, $2, ... for parameters.

params.description: Positional parameter values bound to $1, $2, ... placeholders.

tools.name: list_schemas
tools.title: List schemas
tools.description: List every schema in the connected database. Start here when exploring an unfamiliar database, then call list_tables for the schema you care about. Returns {schemas: [name, ...]}.

tools.name: list_tables
tools.title: List tables
tools.description: List all tables in a schema (default: 'public'). Use this before querying tables you have not seen yet, then call describe_table for column details. Returns {tables: [name, ...]}.

tools.name: describe_table
tools.title: Describe a table
tools.description: Show the structure of one table: column names, data types, nullability, defaults, and primary-key membership. Call this before writing non-trivial queries against a table. Returns {columns: [{column, type, nullable, default, is_primary_key}, ...]}.
